title: Sparse embedding bucket econ notes
body:
Goal: quick scratchpad to reason about pricing sparse/occasional embedding workloads via bucketization. Focus: small-to-medium customers who sporadically call embeddings (search index updates, occasional vector ops).

Principles to keep in mind:
- Make buckets simple (e.g., 1k, 10k, 100k vectors/mo) with clear per-month price and per-excess vector rate.
- Reflect backend cost: GPU/CPU time for embedding generation, storage & retrieval (ANN index costs), and read/write IO.
- Encourage batching + async for cost efficiency: discount for batched ingest.
- Avoid surprising overage bills: allow soft cap and auto-throttle.

Assumptions / microcosts (back-of-envelope):
- Model: small embedding model (float16) ~ 0.00008 GPU-seconds per vector when batched well. (ballpark for medium LLM-based embedder on Ampere-like instance).
- Effective GPU-hour cost to Redwood (amortized infra + op): $6.50 / GPU-hour on reserved capacity. (varies by region).
- Storage: 1536-dim float16 vector = 3 KB compressed/row (rounded). Storage + index + ops amortized: $0.00001 / vector-month for 100k+ scale.
- ANN query cost (per query): negligible compared to embed creation if query only, but when we do online embed generation per query add ~0.00002 GPU-seconds.

Convert GPU-sec to $:
- $6.50 / hour -> $6.50 / 3600s = $0.0018056 / s (per GPU).
- 0.00008 s per vector -> 0.00008 * 0.0018056 = $1.44448e-7 per vector = $0.00000014445 (~1.44e-7 $).
- Round up to $0.00000015 per vector purely for compute.
- For safety margin + infra overhead, set compute contribution = $0.0000003 / vector.

Breakdown candidates (per-vector):
- Compute (amortized): $0.00000030
- Storage (monthly): $0.00001000 (for small scales this will dominate) -> note: we can amortize storage across months, but initial bucket price must cover first-month storage + compute
- Indexing/ops: $0.00000100 (ANN builds, reindex windows)
- Margin/overheads/support: $0.00000300
- Total ~ $0.00001430 per vector first-month (dominant term is storage at tiny scale).

Bucket pricing idea (simple, example numbers):
- Free tier: 500 vectors / month free (activation, testing).
- Nano bucket: up to 5k vectors/mo = $5/mo -> implicit unit price = $0.001 / vector (covers storage + ops + margin)
- Micro bucket: up to 25k vectors/mo = $15/mo -> unit ~ $0.0006 / vector
- Growth bucket: up to 100k vectors/mo = $45/mo -> unit ~ $0.00045 / vector
- Enterprise/Volume: custom pricing > 100k vectors with thresholds and committed discounts (e.g., $0.0002 / vector at 1M+)

Observations: first-month cost is storage-heavy, so buckets should be monthly and include storage for active items. If customers keep vectors across months, long tail storage economics improve unit price over time. We can present bucket as: "ingest price" (covers compute + first-month storage) then a recurring storage fee per vector-month (tiny). But simpler is inclusive monthly buckets.

Example scenario calculations:
1) Small app: 8k new vectors in month 1, then 2k new vectors each subsequent month.
- If on Nano (5k) they'd pay overage. With Micro (25k $15/mo) cost = $15/mo inclusive. Effective first-month per-vector = $15 / 8000 = $0.001875.
- Long-run after 6 months (~8k + 5*2k = 18k) effective per-vector/month ~ $15/18k = $0.00083 (amortized, not precise accounting)

2) Search index re-ingest burst: 120k vectors one-off (backfill).
- If priced per-vector ingest at $0.0007 compute+index+ops, cost = $84. If packaged as one-off bulk ingest product (e.g., $60-$120 depending on SLA) seems sensible. We can offer a bulk-ingest discount for one-shot large uploads: tiered pricing: 0-50k: base rate, 50-200k: -25%, >200k: custom.

Marginal and behavioral levers:
- Batch size discounts: if user sends >100 vectors per request give 20% discount on compute portion (encourages batching).
- Async ingestion discount (no tight SLO) because it lets us schedule cheaper infra.
- Warm cache / hot-query surcharge: charge small per-query premium if embedding computed on read at low-latency SLO (e.g., near real-time webhook).
- TTL-based storage discounts: if user sets auto-delete/TTL < 30 days offer a lower storage rate.

Accounting caveats and TODOs:
- Need real telemetry: average vectors per request, effective batching distribution, median GPU-sec per vector across models.
- Storage numbers here are approximate; actual index overhead for HNSW/IVF depends heavily on params. Need sample budgets across 10k, 100k, 1M scales.
- API-side rate-limits interact with pricing (if we encourage batching, soft quotas should surface in SDK).

UX / product choices (how to present to user):
- Option A: pre-bundled buckets (clean, easy) + clear overage rate. Good for PLG.
- Option B: two-part pricing: ingest fee + storage fee per vector-month. More accurate but harder to grasp. Provide calculator.
- Option C: seat-based plus vector allowances for teams where usage is team-driven. Might fit enterprise buyers.

Packaging experiments to run (A/B candidates):
- A1: Micro bucket ($15/25k) + 20% batch discount for >100 vectors/request. Track conversion vs payg.
- A2: Ingest-only pricing + monthly storage (lower sticker but higher ongoing cost). See churn impact.
- A3: Flat per-month index+query seat for search app: e.g., $50/mo includes 50k vectors + 100k queries/mo. Queries above tier charged tiny per-query.

Short-run ops policy suggestions:
- Always include a "preview cost" on large uploads with an estimated bill.
- Provide a one-click bulk-ingest discount request for >200k vectors to push sale into SE flow.
- Auto-throttle and notify on 80%/95% of bucket. Offer temporary burst credits (small) for trial friction removal.

Open questions to resolve before final proposals:
- Real GPU-sec per vector by model (run bench harness across prod models).
- Accurate storage+index overhead per scale point (10k/100k/1M).
- Typical churn for vectors in customers: what fraction are long-lived?
- Query cost modeling: how to price read-heavy apps vs write-heavy apps?

Notes to self (action items):
- Run quick Jupyter with sample 100k vectors to measure index size with our default HNSW config. (assign to Diego)
- Extract telemetry: mean vectors/request and percentile batch sizes (Maya)
- Prototype a simple price calculator widget for Console that shows estimated monthly cost for selected bucket vs payg
- Draft a short FAQ for product page explaining bucket vs ingest+storage model

Quick mental heuristics to keep pricing anchored:
- At tiny scales (<25k) storage dominates; buckets should be > $10 to cover fixed infra per-customer overheads.
- At mid-scale (25k-500k), amortized compute matters more; we can aggressively lower per-vector price if commitments exist.
- For big enterprise (>1M) move to committed bandwidth (reserve GPU-hours) with a floor price.

Random brainstorms worth keeping:
- "Cold archive" bucket: store vectors at much cheaper storage (S3-like) and rebuild index on demand (good for dormant corpora). Charge low storage + higher revive fee.
- "Vector lifecycle rules" UI: TTLs, cold/archive policies, auto-compress (quantize) after 30 days to reduce storage cost and provide discounted tier.
- Offer embed-as-a-service: we run daily batch jobs for customers (cheaper than on-demand) for scheduled pipelines.

End notes: this is a rough personal scratchpad. Need to run numbers on real telemetry before any external comms. Keep buckets simple for first go; provide advanced two-part model in Console for power users.
